newsitem.title: CHINA: China approves urea, synthetic ammonia plant.
newsitem.headline: China approves urea, synthetic ammonia plant.

text.p: China's cabinet has approved construction of a chemical plant in eastern Nanjing city that will produce 300,000 tonnes of synthetic ammonia and 520,000 tonnes of urea a year, the China News Service said on Thursday.
The Nanjing Chemical Industry (Group) Corp would build the plant, which would cost more than 3.0 billion yuan and go into production in 1999, the agency said but gave no details.

The project in Nanjing, capital of eastern Jiangsu province, was a key part of China's 1996-2000 five-year plan and the construction had been approved recently by the State Council, or cabinet, it said.

Current production of urea in Jiangsu was only around 700,000 tonnes a year, far short of annual consumption in the province of 1.5 million tonnes for agricultural use alone, it said, adding the new plant was expected to improve the situation.
